Q5.question: Q5 — Which neighbourhoods are saturated, and which are emerging hotspots?
Q5.method: Saturated = composite of high density + entire-home share + commercial-host share + occupancy. Emerging = top active-listing growth (recent 6 mo vs prior 6 mo). Member 3 will replace the saturated heuristic with the proper KMeans cluster label.
Q5.policy_guidance: Saturated areas need SUSTAINED presence to prevent backslide. Emerging areas benefit from PRE-EMPTIVE action — intervention is cheaper and more politically tractable before saturation sets in.

Q6.question: Q6 — How does STR pressure compare between Barcelona and London?
Q6.method: Side-by-side comparison of citywide totals and neighbourhood-level medians.
Q6.policy_guidance: Barcelona's RESIDE phase-out is the stronger regulatory instrument and is reflected in lower commercialisation per neighbourhood. London's 90-night cap is comparatively permissive — use this contrast when sizing the political ambition of any proposed change.

Q7.question: Q7 — If entire-home listings were capped at X nights/year, how many listings and which neighbourhoods would be affected?
Q7.method: Sum of breach_count_{cap} per city (city totals), plus top-impacted neighbourhoods per cap per city. RESIDE simulation: count of reside_unregistered listings per Barcelona neighbourhood (entire homes without registration on record).
Q7.policy_guidance: Q7 is the flagship policy decision. The cap-level choice should be sized to enforcement capacity, not theoretical recovery — under-resourced enforcement erodes regulatory credibility. Sequence rollout starting with tier-1 neighbourhoods to maximise early signal.

barcelona.note: Sum over neighbourhoods; excludes listings with no subdivision/neighborhood. City-wide totals from listings_features may differ by a few listings.

london.note: Sum over neighbourhoods; excludes listings with no subdivision/neighborhood. City-wide totals from listings_features may differ by a few listings.
